title: Why trust you?
header_line: My analysis of one book on authority and personal brand. Not a summary of the book. Not affiliated with or endorsed by the author or publisher.

lines.text: I said that the call itself shows part of the book's message: why should you trust me? A student said: because of your background in the business world, and you have things I want in the future, so I view you as an authority. Another said: you talk with powerful words, and it comes across as trustworthy.
A student said: I would trust you because of what you have shown in the past. I said: the past predicts the future. Another added: your past and current relationships, personal and business.
I said that I like to analyze the speed of trust: you could meet someone for ten minutes and, from how they speak and what they say, find them credible. It is pragmatic, tangible and actionable.

I said that high trust and high speed mean a lower cost to acquire a customer, because people come to you since your message is loud and clear. I called it exponential. This is my claim and is to be verified.

I asked: think of the person you trust most and describe that relationship. A student answered: a sibling, who is a serious and solid support system and tells you straight whether it is a good idea or a bad idea. It is never hostile, always constructive.
I said: because he is constructive, he cares about you. One of the greatest leadership traits is to authentically care about each individual in the company.
Who do you trust most, and what do they do that earns it?

exercise.title: Five minutes
steps: Write why someone should trust you.
Write the proof from your past.
Write who you trust most and why.
Write how you show you care about each person you lead.

check.q: What did I say predicts the future?
What did I say I like to analyze?
What did I say is one of the greatest leadership traits?

recap: Know why people should trust you. Show your record. Care about each person.
